subject: Mythology
title: The Sacred Animals of Egypt
description: Learn The Sacred Animals of Egypt in one minute.

hook.text: Egyptians worshipped cats, crocodiles, and ibises as living representatives of the gods on earth.

buildup.text: Bastet was a cat goddess of home and protection. Killing a cat, even by accident, was punishable by death.

discovery.text: Sobek, the crocodile god, had temples where live crocodiles were adorned with gold and fed by priests.

twist.text: Millions of animals were mummified as offerings. Archaeologists found entire catacombs filled with mummified cats.

climax.text: These animal cults lasted thousands of years, showing how deeply Egyptians wove nature into their religion.

punchline.text: In Egypt, the cat was not a pet. It was a prayer.

quiz.question: What was the punishment for killing a cat in ancient Egypt?
options: A fine of gold paid to the temple
Death, even if the killing was accidental
Banishment from the city for seven years
